tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Plan and billing: the server's pages in an in-app sheet, Delete account, the server's price line

Get more credits, in the composer and on Preferences › Account, no longer
opens a pricing address in the browser. It opens a modal sheet over the
window it came from (Shell/ServerSheet). The sheet asks the JusPrin server
for a one-time sign-in link (POST /ent/jusprin/v2/web_link with
{page, from}) and loads it, so the server's page opens signed in as the
app's account. The sheet has a title row with Open in browser and close,
a loading line, and a "Couldn't load" state with Try again after 20 s or a
load error. It closes when the page reaches /ent/jusprin/v2/web/done, on
Escape, or on close, and the account's credits are read again either way.

Preferences › Account gains a last group, Delete account. Its confirmation
shows the server's delete_warning sentence (with a fallback). Confirming
sends delete_account to the host, which sends DELETE /ent/jusprin/v2/account;
on a 204 it removes the account's saved key the way Sign out does and
answers account_deleted. A failure keeps the dialog open and says so.
The host refuses while a reply or a key check is running.

The plan line on Account shows the server's plan.price_line before
"Renews …", so the app carries no price wording of its own.

Tests: AgentUI tests for the price line and the delete flow, a host test
that a delete signs out only after the server has deleted the account, and
a shell harness mode, --server-sheet [capture-dir], that runs both flows
against a real server with a throwaway account's token
(JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL, JUSPRIN_TEST_ACCOUNT_TOKEN).
EOF
git log --oneline -2

I've committed the JusPrin app side of plan and billing on branch `claude/plan-billing` as commit 4e5b107c06, on top of the current `ui-walkthrough` tip. It isn't pushed.

**What the app does now**
- **Get more credits:** clicking it in the chat box or on Preferences › Account opens a sheet inside the app instead of a browser tab. The app gets a one-time sign-in link from the server, so the server's page opens already signed in. The sheet has "Open in browser" and close buttons, a loading line, and a "Couldn't load" message with Try again. It closes when the server's page goes to the "done" address, and the app then reads your credits again.
- **Delete account:** this is now the last group on Preferences › Account. The confirmation dialog shows the server's own sentence, for example "The 500 credits left on … are removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account. This can't be undone." Once the server confirms the delete, the app signs out the same way Sign out does. If the delete fails, the dialog stays open and says so.
- **Price line:** the plan line on Account now shows the server's price sentence, such as "$20 a month.", followed by "Renews …". The app has no price wording of its own.

**Testing**
- All test suites and type checks pass: AgentUI, HomeUI, agent_bridge_tests and jusprin_tests.
- I added a mode to the shell test harness that runs both flows in the real app against staging with a throwaway account. It passed twice:
  - The sheet opened the prices page signed in and closed at the done address.
  - Delete account removed the account on staging and signed out.
- Both throwaway accounts are gone from staging.
- I took screenshots of the delete dialog and the sheet. The sheet's page is a plain "Not Found" because the server's prices and billing pages haven't been built yet. The sheet counts a 404 as a loaded page, so nobody sees a "Couldn't load" message for it.

**Still open**
- The server's prices and billing pages don't exist yet, so Get more credits shows "Not Found" on staging today.
- The canvas board says 20% off with Obico Premium, but JusPrin v1 gives 30%.
- That discount never applies in practice. A JusPrin 2 account is a separate user from an Obico account, so the server never finds a Premium plan on it.

**Decision needed:** should I build the boards marked only "Proposal" as drawn? They are:
- the "Billing and usage" button on Account;
- the "+1,000 credits" line;
- "See prices" on the welcome screen.

The sheet's loading and can't-load states also follow a Proposal board, and I built those because the sheet needs them. Building the rest as drawn means about half a day of app work, plus the server's billing page for the button to open. Leaving them for now costs nothing and keeps what's committed as it is. My pick is to wait until the server's prices and billing pages exist, because the button and links would only lead to "Not Found" today. Do you want them built now, or later?

**Decision needed:** should usage stay on Preferences › Account until the server's Billing and usage page exists? Today Account shows "Usage: N credits in the last 30 days" and there's no Billing and usage button. Moving usage to the server page means deleting it from the app once that page ships. Keeping it on Account means no gap in the meantime. My pick is to keep it on Account for now. Is that right?

The only contract to keep backward compatible.

jusprinv2.obico.io, changes any day.

The plan in dollars, change and cancel, Chargebee’s portal for payment method and invoices, auto-reload, credits used per day and per chat.

"""The credit ledger: lots of credits and what each charged turn took from them.

Balance is the sum of the lots still live, never a stored number, and a lot's
expiry is a comparison at read and charge time, so a lot simply stops counting.
"""
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models


class CreditGrant(models.Model):
    """One lot of credits."""
    PACK = 'pack'
    SUBSCRIPTION = 'subscription'
    SIGNUP = 'signup'
    FREE = 'free'
    REWARD = 'reward'
    LAUNCH_BONUS = 'launch_bonus'
    KINDS = [(k, k) for k in (PACK, SUBSCRIPTION, SIGNUP, FREE, REWARD, LAUNCH_BONUS)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    kind = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=KINDS)
    credits_granted = models.IntegerField()
    credits_remaining = models.IntegerField()
    expires_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)  # null: never
    # What makes the lot one of a kind for this person: signup, free:<n>,
    # report:<print report id>, and the invoice and subscription refs of billing.
    source_ref = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'source_ref'], name='jusprin_credit_grant_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'expires_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.source_ref}: {self.credits_remaining}/{self.credits_granted}'


class CreditCharge(models.Model):
    """One per charged turn. credits is 0 for a basic turn on a plan that includes
    them, and for a turn the app started."""
    BASIC = 'basic'
    EXPERT = 'expert'
    TIERS = [(BASIC, BASIC), (EXPERT, EXPERT)]
    PERSON = 'person'
    APP = 'app'
    ORIGINS = [(PERSON, PERSON), (APP, APP)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    turn_id = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    chat_id = models.CharField(max_length=32, null=True, blank=True)
    alias = models.CharField(max_length=64)
    tier = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=TIERS)
    credits = models.IntegerField()
    origin = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=ORIGINS)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'turn_id'], name='jusprin_credit_charge_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'created_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.turn_id}: {self.credits}'


class CreditAllocation(models.Model):
    """Which lots paid a charge."""
    charge = models.ForeignKey(CreditCharge, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='allocations')
    grant = models.ForeignKey(CreditGrant, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='allocations')
    credits = models.IntegerField()


class PrintReport(models.Model):
    """What a person says about how a sliced print came out: the training-data
    channel, so it has its own table rather than a place in the gateway's chats."""
    WORKED = 'worked'
    PARTLY = 'partly'
    FAILED = 'failed'
    OUTCOMES = [(k, k) for k in (WORKED, PARTLY, FAILED)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    gcode_hash = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    outcome = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=OUTCOMES)
    text = models.TextField()
    # Sent by the app with the report: printer, material, process, slice
    # statistics, manufacturing input hash, and the project's name for the row.
    facts = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)
    photos = models.JSONField(default=list)  # the stored photos' URLs
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'gcode_hash'], name='jusprin_print_report_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'created_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.gcode_hash}: {self.outcome}'


class PrintReportReview(models.Model):
    """A person at Obico read the report."""
    report = models.OneToOneField(PrintReport, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    invalid = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    note = models.CharField(max_length=500, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
"""What GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account answers: numbers and names, so the app can
keep reading it for years, and the few sentences about money the app shows word
for word, so no price or plan wording is in the app's code."""
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Count, Sum
from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone

from app_ent.models import Subscription
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .ledger import active_v2_plan, ensure_lots, live_lots
from .models import CreditCharge, CreditGrant
from .reports import report_activity

USAGE_DAYS = 30


def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    return {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }


def _dollars(cents: int) -> str:
    return f'${cents // 100}' if cents % 100 == 0 else f'${cents / 100:.2f}'


def _price_line(spec: Dict, obico_discount: bool) -> str:
    if not obico_discount:
        return f"{_dollars(spec['cents'])} a month."
    percent = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT
    return f"{_dollars(spec['cents'] * (100 - percent) // 100)} a month with Obico Premium’s {percent}% off."


def _plan(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    subscription = Subscription.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    obico_discount = bool(subscription and subscription.active())
    return {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': obico_discount,
        'auto_reload': False,
        'price_line': _price_line(spec, obico_discount),
    }


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def _usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    # The gateway never sees a chat's title, so a row names the chat by its id.
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'tier': row['tier'],
                 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity += report_activity(user, now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def _delete_warning(user, plan: Optional[Dict], credits: int) -> str:
    """What Delete account's confirmation says."""
    left = f"{credits:,} credit{'' if credits == 1 else 's'} left on {user.email} {'is' if credits == 1 else 'are'}"
    if plan and credits:
        gone = f"Your {plan['name']} plan ends today, and the {left} removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account."
    elif plan:
        gone = f"Your {plan['name']} plan ends today, and everything JusPrin keeps for {user.email} is removed."
    elif credits:
        gone = f'The {left} removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account.'
    else:
        gone = f'Everything JusPrin keeps for {user.email} is removed.'
    return f'{gone} This can\u2019t be undone.'


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or lot.expires_at is not None]
    total = sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots)
    plan = _plan(user)
    return {
        'credits': {'total': total, 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': plan,
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': _usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
        'delete_warning': _delete_warning(user, plan, total),
    }

"""What GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account answers: numbers and names, so the app can
keep reading it for years, and the few sentences about money the app shows word
for word, so no price or plan wording is in the app's code."""
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Count, Sum
from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone

from app_ent.models import Subscription
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .ledger import active_v2_plan, ensure_lots, live_lots
from .models import CreditCharge, CreditGrant
from .reports import report_activity

USAGE_DAYS = 30


def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    return {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }


def _dollars(cents: int) -> str:
    return f'${cents // 100}' if cents % 100 == 0 else f'${cents / 100:.2f}'


def _price_line(spec: Dict, obico_discount: bool) -> str:
    if not obico_discount:
        return f"{_dollars(spec['cents'])} a month."
    percent = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT
    return f"{_dollars(spec['cents'] * (100 - percent) // 100)} a month with Obico Premium’s {percent}% off."


def _plan(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    subscription = Subscription.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    obico_discount = bool(subscription and subscription.active())
    return {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': obico_discount,
        'auto_reload': False,
        'price_line': _price_line(spec, obico_discount),
    }


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def _usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    # The gateway never sees a chat's title, so a row names the chat by its id.
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'tier': row['tier'],
                 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity += report_activity(user, now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def _delete_warning(user, plan: Optional[Dict], credits: int) -> str:
    """What Delete account's confirmation says."""
    left = f"{credits:,} credit{'' if credits == 1 else 's'} left on {user.email} {'is' if credits == 1 else 'are'}"
    if plan and credits:
        gone = f"Your {plan['name']} plan ends today, and the {left} removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account."
    elif plan:
        gone = f"Your {plan['name']} plan ends today, and everything JusPrin keeps for {user.email} is removed."
    elif credits:
        gone = f'The {left} removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account.'
    else:
        gone = f'Everything JusPrin keeps for {user.email} is removed.'
    return f'{gone} This can\u2019t be undone.'


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or lot.expires_at is not None]
    total = sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots)
    plan = _plan(user)
    return {
        'credits': {'total': total, 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': plan,
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': _usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
        'delete_warning': _delete_warning(user, plan, total),
    }

"""Charging a turn against a person's lots of credits.

Every credit is the same. A turn costs its alias's price, except a turn the app
started by itself (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) and a basic
message on an active Workshop plan, which cost nothing.
"""
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Optional

from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.db import transaction
from django.db.models import F, Q
from django.utils import timezone

from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .models import CreditAllocation, CreditCharge, CreditGrant


class CreditsExhausted(Exception):
    """The next turn cannot be paid."""

    def __init__(self, balance: int, cost: int, plan: Optional[str]):
        super().__init__(f'{cost} credits needed, {balance} available')
        self.balance = balance
        self.cost = cost
        self.plan = plan

    def details(self) -> Dict:
        return {'balance': self.balance, 'cost': self.cost, 'plan': self.plan}


def _is_subscribed(user_id: int) -> bool:
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=user_id).first()
    return plan is not None and plan.is_active and (
        plan.plan_id in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS or plan.plan_id in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS)


def has_paid(user_id: int) -> bool:
    """Subscribed now, or ever granted a plan's or a credit pack's credits."""
    return _is_subscribed(user_id) or CreditGrant.objects.filter(
        user_id=user_id, kind__in=(CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION, CreditGrant.PACK)).exists()


def ensure_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime = None) -> None:
    """Creates the lots nobody buys: the first month's, once per account, and
    after it the free credits of an account without a subscription, a new lot
    once the last one has expired. Each lasts a month from the day it is granted.
    Lazy, in place of a monthly sweep over every account. Concurrent requests meet
    on the unique source_ref."""
    now = now or timezone.now()
    signup, _ = CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref='signup', defaults={
        'kind': CreditGrant.SIGNUP,
        'credits_granted': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': now + relativedelta(months=1),
    })
    if now < signup.expires_at or _is_subscribed(user_id):
        return
    free = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, kind=CreditGrant.FREE)
    if free.filter(expires_at__gt=now).exists():
        return
    CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref=f'free:{free.count() + 1}', defaults={
        'kind': CreditGrant.FREE,
        'credits_granted': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_CREDITS,
        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': now + relativedelta(months=1),
    })


def live_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime):
    """The lots still counting, in draw order: the soonest to expire first,
    never-expiring last, oldest first within one expiry."""
    return (CreditGrant.objects
            .filter(Q(expires_at__isnull=True) | Q(expires_at__gt=now), user_id=user_id)
            .order_by(F('expires_at').asc(nulls_last=True), 'created_at', 'id'))


def lock_person(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Serialises everything that spends a person's lots, until the transaction
    ends. On the person's row because they may hold no live lot. no_key lets a new
    lot or charge pointing at that row go ahead."""
    get_user_model().objects.select_for_update(no_key=True).only('pk').get(pk=user_id)


def active_v2_plan(user_id: int) -> Optional[JusPrinPlan]:
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=user_id).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS:
        return None
    return plan


def _price(alias, origin, plan) -> int:
    if origin == CreditCharge.APP:
        return 0
    if alias.tier == CreditCharge.BASIC and plan and settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id].get('unlimited_basic'):
        return 0
    return alias.credits


def charge_turn(user_id: int, turn_id: str, alias, origin: str, chat_id: str = None) -> CreditCharge:
    """Charges a turn once, whatever retries its first request. Raises
    CreditsExhausted with nothing written when the lots cannot pay."""
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user_id, now)
    with transaction.atomic():
        lock_person(user_id)
        existing = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, turn_id=turn_id).first()
        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        lots = list(live_lots(user_id, now))
        plan = active_v2_plan(user_id)
        cost = _price(alias, origin, plan)
        balance = sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots)
        if balance < cost:
            raise CreditsExhausted(balance, cost, plan.plan_id if plan else None)

        charge = CreditCharge.objects.create(user_id=user_id, turn_id=turn_id, chat_id=chat_id, alias=alias.id,
                                             tier=alias.tier, credits=cost, origin=origin)
        left = cost
        for lot in lots:
            if left == 0:
                break
            if lot.credits_remaining <= 0:
                continue
            taken = min(left, lot.credits_remaining)
            lot.credits_remaining -= taken
            lot.save(update_fields=['credits_remaining'])
            CreditAllocation.objects.create(charge=charge, grant=lot, credits=taken)
            left -= taken
    return charge

"""

This module contains all JusPrin-specific Chargebee integration logic including:
- Checkout URL generation
- Callback handling
- Webhook processing
- Subscription management

Keeps the main cb_views.py clean and focused on core subscription logic.
"""

import json
from django.utils import timezone
from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect

# JusPrin Constants
OBICO_PRO_DISCOUNT_COUPON = 'gRpFfWHgARQSCkC0ZNR74ico'
OBICO_PRO_DISCOUNT_PERCENTAGE = 30  # 30% discount for Obico Pro subscribers


def is_jusprin_subscription(plan_id):
    """
    Check if a plan_id belongs to a JusPrin subscription

    Args:
        plan_id (str): The Chargebee plan ID

    Returns:
        bool: True if this is a jusprin subscription
    """
    return plan_id.startswith('jusprin-unlimited-')



@login_required
def jusprin_cb_callback(request):
    """
    Dedicated JusPrin subscription callback handler

    This is completely decoupled from the Obico subscription system.

    Args:
        request: Django request object with 'id' parameter for hosted page

    Returns:
        HttpResponse: Redirect response to pricing page with success parameter
    """
    cb_page = chargebee.HostedPage.retrieve(request.GET['id'])
    if cb_page.hosted_page.state != 'succeeded':
        raise Exception("JusPrin checkout failed")

    plan_id = cb_page.hosted_page.content.subscription.plan_id

    # Verify this is actually a JusPrin subscription
    if not is_jusprin_subscription(plan_id):
        raise Exception(f"Invalid plan ID for JusPrin callback: {plan_id}")

    # Process the subscription
    upsert_jusprin_plan(cb_page.hosted_page.content.subscription.values, request.user)

    # Redirect back to JusPrin pricing page with success indicator
    return redirect('/ent/jusprin/pricing/?checkout=success')


@csrf_exempt
def jusprin_cb_webhook(request):
    """
    Dedicated JustPrint subscription webhook handler

    This is completely decoupled from the Obico webhook system.

    Args:
        request: Django request object with webhook payload

    Returns:
        HttpResponse: Empty response indicating successful processing
    """
    SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS = [
        'subscription_created', 'subscription_started', 'subscription_activated',
        'subscription_changed', 'subscription_cancellation_scheduled',
        'subscription_cancelled', 'subscription_reactivated', 'subscription_renewed'
    ]

    payload = request.body
    cb_event = json.loads(payload)

    if cb_event['event_type'] in SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS:
        cb_sub = cb_event['content']['subscription']

        # Verify this is actually a JusPrin subscription
        if not is_jusprin_subscription(cb_sub['plan_id']):
            return HttpResponse('')  # Ignore non-JustPrint subscriptions

        # Find user by subscription ID first, fallback to email
        try:
            user = JusPrinPlan.objects.get(external_id=cb_sub['id']).user
        except JusPrinPlan.DoesNotExist:
            try:
                user = User.objects.get(email__iexact=cb_event['content']['customer']['email'])
            except User.DoesNotExist:
                # Log error but don't crash - this could be a test webhook
                return HttpResponse('')

        upsert_jusprin_plan(cb_sub, user)

    return HttpResponse('')


def handle_jusprin_webhook(cb_event):

    cb_sub = cb_event['content']['subscription']

    try:

    except JusPrinPlan.DoesNotExist:
        try:

@login_required
def generate_jusprin_checkout_url(request):
    """
    Generate Chargebee checkout URL for JusPrin Unlimited subscription

    Args:
        request: Django request object with GET parameters:

    Returns:

    """
    user = request.user
    billing_cycle = 'annual' if request.GET.get('annual', 'false').lower() == 'true' else 'monthly'

    # Check if user has active Obico Pro subscription and automatically apply coupon
    coupon_id = None
    if hasattr(user, 'subscription') and user.subscription and user.subscription.external_id:
        try:
            cb_subscription = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(user.subscription.external_id)
            if cb_subscription.subscription.status == 'active':
                # Apply discount coupon for Obico Pro subscribers
                coupon_id = OBICO_PRO_DISCOUNT_COUPON
        except:
            # If we can't verify Obico subscription, proceed without coupon
            pass

    # Use the plan IDs specified: jusprin-unlimited-monthly and jusprin-unlimited-annual
    plan_id = f'jusprin-unlimited-{billing_cycle}'

    # Check if user already has a JusPrin subscription
    if hasattr(user, 'jusprinplan') and user.jusprinplan.external_id and chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(user.jusprinplan.external_id).subscription.status == 'active':
        # Update existing subscription
        subscription_payload = {
            "id": user.jusprinplan.external_id,
            "plan_id": plan_id,
        }

        checkout_payload = {
            "subscription": subscription_payload,
            "redirect_url": request.build_absolute_uri("/ent/jusprin/cb_callback/"),
        }

        # Add coupon if provided
        if coupon_id:
            checkout_payload["coupon_ids"] = [coupon_id]

        result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_existing(checkout_payload)

    else:
        # Create new subscription
        checkout_payload = {
            "subscription": {
                "plan_id": plan_id,
            },
            "customer": cb_customer_for_user(user),
            "redirect_url": request.build_absolute_uri("/ent/jusprin/cb_callback/"),
        }

        # Add coupon if provided
        if coupon_id:
            checkout_payload["coupon_ids"] = [coupon_id]

        result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_new(checkout_payload)

    # Handle redirect for mobile web view
    if request.GET.get('redirect'):
        return redirect(result._response['hosted_page']['url'])

    return HttpResponse(
        json.dumps(result._response['hosted_page']),
        content_type='application/json',
    )

    Create or update JusPrinPlan based on Chargebee subscription data

    This function handles all subscription status changes including:
    - New subscriptions

            'external_user_id': cb_subscription['customer_id'],
            'plan_id': cb_subscription['plan_id']
        },
    )

    # Update plan with current subscription data
    jusprin_plan.external_id = cb_subscription['id']

# Giving Obico Premium subscribers their JusPrin 2 discount: options (2026-11-07)

Investigation only. Code read on tsd-enterprise `origin/master` (15fdf1e5e0, the code on staging as obi.4086). One read-only query on the local dev database. No production or staging data read.

## What JusPrin 1 does today

JusPrin 1 users sign in with their Obico account, so there is only one user. When they start checkout, `generate_jusprin_checkout_url` in `web_ent/jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py` asks Chargebee whether that user's Obico subscription has status `active`. If it does, it adds Chargebee coupon `gRpFfWHgARQSCkC0ZNR74ico` to the checkout. `OBICO_PRO_DISCOUNT_PERCENTAGE = 30` is the number the pricing page shows. Obico's free 30-day trial has no Chargebee subscription, so trial users do not get the discount. Nothing ever takes the coupon off later, so someone who cancels Premium keeps the discount.

## How JusPrin 2 accounts relate to Obico accounts

Both live in the same database, the same `User` table, on the same server. A user's "syndicate" (a tag saying which brand the account belongs to) is `base` for Obico and `jusprinv2` for JusPrin 2. The server picks the syndicate from the host name, `jusprinv2.obico.io` versus `app.obico.io`. One email can have one account in each, and the test `SubscriptionStatusTestCase` covers exactly that case. You sign in to JusPrin 2 with an emailed code or with Google, so its email addresses are always verified. Obico accounts can be unverified, because the setting is `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION = 'optional'`.

## A bug in the code already on staging

`_plan()` in `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py` treats `Subscription.active()` as Premium. But every new user, JusPrin 2 accounts included, gets a 30-day `pro-trial` row when it is created (`start_free_trial` in `app_ent/models.py`). On local dev, all three JusPrin 2 accounts have one. So for its first 30 days, every JusPrin 2 account counts as Premium. Tests miss this because that signal is switched off when tests run. Nobody sees it yet, because no JusPrin 2 plan can be bought.

## Ways to connect the two accounts

1. **Match on verified email, inside the server.** When someone checks out, and when GET /v2/account runs, look up the `base` account with the same verified address. Give the discount only if that account has a real paid subscription: a Chargebee id and a plan that is not `pro-trial`. This means one function plus tests in tsd-enterprise only. No obico-server or app change. It fails when the person uses a different email for each product. Support could fix that case by hand.
2. **Sign in to Obico once to link the accounts.** A "Link Obico account" button on the server's prices page signs in on app.obico.io and saves a one-to-one link. This covers different emails. It costs several days: an OAuth client for the base syndicate, a link table, and unlinking. Still tsd-enterprise only.
3. **An internal API.** Not needed. Both accounts are in the same database.

Whichever we pick, the discount belongs in the JusPrin 2 checkout. That checkout does not exist yet: `/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices` returns 404. The price line in `_plan()` should use the same check.

## My pick

Option 1, with option 2 held back unless support requests show many people using different emails.

## Decisions

Decision needed: should the JusPrin 2 discount be 20%, as the board says, or 30%, as JusPrin 1 gives? 20% is what the code has now (`JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT`). 30% would match what JusPrin 1 subscribers already know, but costs more per plan. I'd pick 20%, because the board was designed with it.

Decision needed: should someone who cancels Premium lose the JusPrin 2 discount at their next renewal? Keeping it, as JusPrin 1 does, costs nothing to build. Removing it means handling the Obico subscription-cancelled webhook and taking the coupon off the JusPrin 2 subscription in Chargebee. That is about a day of work. I'd pick removing it, because otherwise one month of Premium buys a discount forever.

## Still unknown

- Whether a 20% coupon exists in Chargebee.
- How long the JusPrin 1 coupon lasts.
- How many Premium subscribers have a JusPrin 2 account under the same email. That needs a production query, which I did not run.
- Whether the discount also applies to the Credit pack. My inference is that it applies only to plans, because only the plan price line uses it.

"""Print reports and the credits they earn, granted at once when the automatic
checks pass."""
from typing import Dict, List

from django.conf import settings
from django.db import IntegrityError, transaction

from .models import CreditGrant, PrintReport, PrintReportReview


class ReportRefused(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: str):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.code = code


def _reward_ref(report: PrintReport) -> str:
    return f'report:{report.id}'


def submit_report(user, gcode_hash: str, outcome: str, text: str, facts: Dict, photos: List[str]) -> PrintReport:
    """Stores the report and grants its reward. The caller has checked the text
    and the photos."""
    credits = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_CREDITS
    try:
        with transaction.atomic():
            report = PrintReport.objects.create(user=user, gcode_hash=gcode_hash, outcome=outcome, text=text,
                                                facts=facts, photos=photos)
            CreditGrant.objects.create(user=user, kind=CreditGrant.REWARD, credits_granted=credits,
                                       credits_remaining=credits, source_ref=_reward_ref(report))
    except IntegrityError:
        raise ReportRefused('already_reported')
    return report


def is_reported(user, gcode_hash: str) -> bool:
    return PrintReport.objects.filter(user=user, gcode_hash=gcode_hash).exists()


def review_report(report: PrintReport, invalid: bool, note: str = '') -> PrintReportReview:
    """Records the review. The credits a report earned stay with the person."""
    review, _ = PrintReportReview.objects.update_or_create(report=report, defaults={'invalid': invalid, 'note': note})
    return review


def report_activity(user, since) -> List[Dict]:
    """The Account usage table's rows for reports: what each earned."""
    by_ref = {_reward_ref(report): report for report in PrintReport.objects.filter(user=user)}
    grants = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=since, source_ref__in=by_ref.keys())
    rows = []
    for grant in grants:
        report = by_ref[grant.source_ref]
        rows.append({'date': grant.created_at.date().isoformat(),
                     'title': 'Print report · ' + report.facts.get('project', report.gcode_hash[:8]),
                     'credits': grant.credits_granted, 'kind': 'report'})
    return rows

"""Print reports and the credits they earn, granted at once when the automatic
checks pass."""
from typing import Dict, List

from django.conf import settings
from django.db import IntegrityError, transaction

from .models import CreditGrant, PrintReport, PrintReportReview


class ReportRefused(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: str):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.code = code


def _reward_ref(report: PrintReport) -> str:
    return f'report:{report.id}'


def submit_report(user, gcode_hash: str, outcome: str, text: str, facts: Dict, photos: List[str]) -> PrintReport:
    """Stores the report and grants its reward. The caller has checked the text
    and the photos."""
    credits = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_CREDITS
    try:
        with transaction.atomic():
            report = PrintReport.objects.create(user=user, gcode_hash=gcode_hash, outcome=outcome, text=text,
                                                facts=facts, photos=photos)
            CreditGrant.objects.create(user=user, kind=CreditGrant.REWARD, credits_granted=credits,
                                       credits_remaining=credits, source_ref=_reward_ref(report))
    except IntegrityError:
        raise ReportRefused('already_reported')
    return report


def is_reported(user, gcode_hash: str) -> bool:
    return PrintReport.objects.filter(user=user, gcode_hash=gcode_hash).exists()


def review_report(report: PrintReport, invalid: bool, note: str = '') -> PrintReportReview:
    """Records the review. The credits a report earned stay with the person."""
    review, _ = PrintReportReview.objects.update_or_create(report=report, defaults={'invalid': invalid, 'note': note})
    return review


def report_activity(user, since) -> List[Dict]:
    """The Account usage table's rows for reports: what each earned."""
    by_ref = {_reward_ref(report): report for report in PrintReport.objects.filter(user=user)}
    grants = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=since, source_ref__in=by_ref.keys())
    rows = []
    for grant in grants:
        report = by_ref[grant.source_ref]
        rows.append({'date': grant.created_at.date().isoformat(),
                     'title': 'Print report · ' + report.facts.get('project', report.gcode_hash[:8]),
                     'credits': grant.credits_granted, 'kind': 'report'})
    return rows

"""Makes JusPrin 2 a syndicate of its own on this server: the 'jusprinv2'
syndicate, the site for its host, and Google sign-in on that host. Accounts
made through that host are JusPrin 2's, apart from Obico's (the syndicate is
decided by the host, lib/syndicate.py). Its brand is SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'];
the 'jusprin' brand is JusPrin v1's, shown to v1 on Obico's host. Safe to run
again; it changes only what differs.

    python manage.py set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate jusprinv2-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io
"""
from allauth.socialaccount.models import SocialApp
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.db import transaction

from app.models import Syndicate


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Set up the JusPrin 2 syndicate and the site for its host"

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument('domain', help="JusPrin 2's host, as jusprinv2.obico.io")
        parser.add_argument('--google-from', metavar='DOMAIN',
                            help="the host whose Google sign-in app JusPrin 2's host uses too, as app.obico.io")

    @transaction.atomic
    def handle(self, *args, domain, google_from=None, **kwargs):
        syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(name='jusprinv2')
        site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain=domain, defaults={'name': 'JusPrin'})
        # A new site joins the first syndicate (add_site_to_default_syndicate),
        # and a request takes its site's first syndicate, so the site must be
        # JusPrin 2's alone.
        for other in site.syndicates.exclude(id=syndicate.id):
            other.sites.remove(site)
            self.stdout.write(f'Removed {domain} from the {other.name} syndicate')
        syndicate.sites.add(site)
        self.stdout.write(f'{domain} is the jusprinv2 syndicate\'s site')

        if google_from:
            # Google sign-in stores a person's Google ID with the site's id
            # (site_specific_allauth_google_provider), so on this site it makes
            # JusPrin 2 accounts. allauth refuses a site with two Google apps.
            apps = list(SocialApp.objects.filter(provider='google', sites__domain=google_from))
            if len(apps) != 1:
                raise CommandError(f'{google_from} has {len(apps)} Google sign-in apps, not one')
            apps[0].sites.add(site)
            self.stdout.write(f'Google sign-in app "{apps[0].name}" serves {domain}')
from django.db import models
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from django.dispatch import receiver
from django.db.models.signals import post_save

"""Makes JusPrin 2 a syndicate of its own on this server: the 'jusprinv2'
syndicate, the site for its host, and Google sign-in on that host. Accounts
made through that host are JusPrin 2's, apart from Obico's (the syndicate is
decided by the host, lib/syndicate.py). Its brand is SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'];
the 'jusprin' brand is JusPrin v1's, shown to v1 on Obico's host. Safe to run
again; it changes only what differs.

    python manage.py set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate jusprinv2-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io
"""
from allauth.socialaccount.models import SocialApp
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.db import transaction

from app.models import Syndicate


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Set up the JusPrin 2 syndicate and the site for its host"

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument('domain', help="JusPrin 2's host, as jusprinv2.obico.io")
        parser.add_argument('--google-from', metavar='DOMAIN',
                            help="the host whose Google sign-in app JusPrin 2's host uses too, as app.obico.io")

    @transaction.atomic
    def handle(self, *args, domain, google_from=None, **kwargs):
        syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(name='jusprinv2')
        site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain=domain, defaults={'name': 'JusPrin'})
        # A new site joins the first syndicate (add_site_to_default_syndicate),
        # and a request takes its site's first syndicate, so the site must be
        # JusPrin 2's alone.
        for other in site.syndicates.exclude(id=syndicate.id):
            other.sites.remove(site)
            self.stdout.write(f'Removed {domain} from the {other.name} syndicate')
        syndicate.sites.add(site)
        self.stdout.write(f'{domain} is the jusprinv2 syndicate\'s site')

        if google_from:
            # Google sign-in stores a person's Google ID with the site's id
            # (site_specific_allauth_google_provider), so on this site it makes
            # JusPrin 2 accounts. allauth refuses a site with two Google apps.
            apps = list(SocialApp.objects.filter(provider='google', sites__domain=google_from))
            if len(apps) != 1:
                raise CommandError(f'{google_from} has {len(apps)} Google sign-in apps, not one')
            apps[0].sites.add(site)
            self.stdout.write(f'Google sign-in app "{apps[0].name}" serves {domain}')

the loop nor hold a sync worker, and it must stop the upstream request when the
client disconnects. jusprin.v2.asgi resolves the path with Django's URL conf
and hands requests for these endpoints to GatewayEndpoint.asgi.
"""
